column3: Threat and murder are separate nouns in the Greek; BSB combines them as “murderous threats.”
“Saul” and “replied” make the speakers and speech connection explicit.
The Greek describes his eyes as having been opened; BSB makes the opening his action.
BSB’s “in a vision” matches the Textus Receptus (ὁράματι); the critical text lacks it.
Hearing from many is recast as many people telling him.
“Instrument” renders vessel; “their” is supplied before kings, and “people” renders sons.
“Saul” supplies the pronoun referent at the laying on of hands.
The statement about his arrival is made a question.
The passive disclosure to Saul is made active; “city” is supplied before gates.
“A window” is supplied; the Greek says through the wall.
“Damascus” specifies the road's destination; the city name is then rendered “that city.”
“Saul” supplies the subject; “freely” is supplied with moving about.
